For stride-one causal convolutions, derive receptive-field span from every temporal convolution: R = 1 + Σ(k−1)d; residual shortcuts and 1×1 convolutions do not enlarge it. Block count alone is insufficient. NextItNet implementations differ: Microsoft’s bottleneck block contains one temporal convolution, while RecBole’s block-b contains two, with dilations d and 2d. For k=3 and block dilations [1,2], these yield R=7 versus R=19. These are architectural deductions from the implementations. [Microsoft source](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html), [RecBole source](https://www.recbole.io/docs/v1.1.1/_modules/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/nextitnet.html).

Consequently, with identical weights, deterministic inference, aligned final-item readout and position-local operations, full-history and last-eight representations must coincide when R≤8. When R>8, older interactions can matter, although equality remains possible for particular inputs or weights. Padding differences outside the dependency graph cannot affect the output. Inside it, learned/nonzero padding embeddings, convolution biases and normalization offsets can make padded positions nonzero. Zero input embeddings alone do not guarantee zero hidden padding; physically cropping also introduces fresh layer boundaries. Thus differences may reflect boundary artifacts rather than useful older context. Microsoft’s implementation explicitly includes convolution biases and learned normalization offsets. [Source](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html).

Normalization axes are decisive: Microsoft’s LayerNorm operates across channels separately at each position, preserving temporal locality. Normalization that computes statistics across time can transmit information beyond the convolutional receptive field and make representations depend on padding length; InstanceNorm1d is one example. Verify axes and evaluation behavior, then compare identical-weight outputs while perturbing only items preceding the last eight. Separate branches with different parameters can differ without receiving distinct context. [LayerNorm implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html), [InstanceNorm1d documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.InstanceNorm1d.html).
